text.p: Halliburton Co said on Tuesday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire NUMAR Corp in a stock swap valued at $360 million, or about $39.62 per Numar share.
The news was released just after regular trading hours had ended. NUMAR was unchanged on the day at 20-3/4. Halliburton closed down 1-3/8 to 80-5/8.

Halliburton said in a news release that the deal is expected to be tax-free. The company added that the acquisition should be "modestly dilutive to near-term earnings per share," but not dilutive to earnings in 1998.
Halliburton said it will issue 0.4832 of a share for each outstanding NUMAR share (or 0.9664 of a share if the deal closes after Halliburton's 2-for-1 stock split, also announced Tuesday).
The transaction, which must be approved by regulators and NUMAR shareholders, would involve issuing 4.4 million Halliburton shares, or 8.8 million after the split.

NUMAR, based in Malvern, Pa., makes a patented well logging device, the Magnetic Resonance Imaging Logging tool, or MRIL. It will operate as a wholly owned Halliburton subsidiary, with current management remaining in place.
Halliburton is a diversified energy services, engineering, maintenance and construction company.
